measures.subject: Online sports wagering (constitutional amendment)
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Nebraska Constitution be amended to authorize the enactment of laws allowing persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform when offered by an authorized gaming operator conducting games of chance within a licensed racetrack enclosure in Nebraska?
measures.summary: Would amend the state constitution so that laws may allow people located in Nebraska to place sports wagers online through platforms offered by licensed racetrack gaming operators.

measures.subject: Online sports wagering (statute)
measures.ballotTitle: Shall statutes be enacted that: (1) Allow persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform when offered by an authorized gaming operator conducting games of chance within a licensed racetrack enclosure in Nebraska or the operator’s platform provider; and (2) Regulate such sports wagers?
measures.summary: Would amend the Nebraska Racetrack Gaming Act to allow and regulate online sports wagering by people located in Nebraska through licensed racetrack gaming operators or their platform providers, operative January 1, 2027.

measures.subject: School athletic teams designated by biological sex
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Nebraska Constitution be amended to provide: (1) Schools must expressly designate each athletic team or sport as one of the following based on biological sex: (a) Males, men, or boys; (b) females, women, or girls; or (c) coed or mixed; and (2) Athletic teams or sports designated for females, women, or girls shall not be open to students of the male sex? The amendment would apply to all athletic teams or sports sponsored by public schools or postsecondary educational institutions, and private schools or educational institutions whose athletic teams or sports compete against public schools or institutions.
measures.summary: Would amend the state constitution to require schools to designate each athletic team as male, female, or coed by biological sex and to bar male students from teams designated for females.

measures.subject: Legislative term limits
measures.ballotTitle: A constitutional amendment to change the limit on legislative terms from two consecutive terms to three consecutive terms.
measures.summary: Would amend Article III, section 12 of the state constitution to let state senators serve three consecutive terms, instead of two, before becoming ineligible for four years.

measureEffectiveNote: Initiatives (Neb. Const. Art. III, sec. 4): a measure passes with a majority of votes cast on it that is at least 35% of the total vote cast, and 'shall take effect upon proclamation by the Governor which shall be made within ten days after the official canvass of such votes' (so between Nov 30 and Dec 10, 2026). Legislative amendments (Art. XVI, sec. 1): an amendment adopted by a majority (with the same 35% floor) 'shall become a part of this Constitution', with no separate date. The Board of State Canvassers meets to certify results on November 30, 2026 (4th Monday after the election, Neb. Rev. Stat. 32-1037, per the SOS 2026 Election Calendar); used here as the representative date. Initiative 441's statutory changes become operative January 1, 2027 (its Sec. 4).
notes: Candidates and parties are from the Nebraska SOS 'Final Statewide General Candidate List', dated 9/11/2026. Parties appear there as 'Republican', 'Democratic', 'Libertarian', 'Legal Marijuana NOW', 'Nebraska Working People', 'America First', and 'By Petition' for petition candidates; they are kept as listed.
U.S. Senate: no Democratic candidate is listed. Independent Dan Osborn is listed as 'By Petition'.
NE-2 is an open seat. The list shows no incumbent; Brinker Harding (R), Denise Powell (D), and Eric Michael Foreman (Libertarian) are listed.
Gov / Lt Gov tickets are listed as 'X and Y' on the SOS list and written here as 'X / Y'.

Not included as statewide: the nonpartisan Legislature (even-numbered districts, 46 filings), Public Service Commissioner (district races, 2 filings), and judicial retention (separate SOS list dated 8/3/2026).

Initiatives 440, 441 and 442 have their ballot language (the 'Shall ...' question) from the SOS 2026 Ballot Measures Pamphlet. Each title is preceded on the ballot by 'A vote FOR ... / A vote AGAINST ...' explanatory statements, which are left out of ballotTitle. LR19CA's ballot language is set verbatim by Sec. 2 of the resolution.
Polls close at 8 PM CST in Central-time counties and 7 PM MST in Mountain-time counties (Neb. Rev. Stat. 32-908, per the SOS calendar). Both are 02:00 UTC on Nov 4, 2026.
